records.programme_name: Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung Scholarship - Funding for International Students and Doctoral Candidates from Abroad
records.program_type: Study and doctoral scholarship (politically oriented foundation)
records.deadline_note: For international students and doctoral candidates from abroad: the online application period is 15 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET). For applicants educated in Germany, the application period is 15 June 2027 to 15 July 2027 (12:00 CEST).
records.application_cycle: Two application rounds: 15 December 2026 - 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET) for international applicants, and 15 June 2027 - 15 July 2027 (12:00 CEST) for applicants educated in Germany
records.status_note: The application window for the study scholarships for international students and doctoral candidates from abroad runs from 15 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET). Applicants from abroad should contact the HSS Abroad Office (Auslandsbüro) in their home country, or use the online application. There is no legal entitlement to the stated benefits and the scholarship does not have to be repaid.
records.duration: Spans the study period; doctoral funding maximum 1,750 euros per month plus a 100 euro research-cost allowance

Doctoral scholarships: maximum rate of 1,750 euros per month plus a research-cost allowance of 100 euros, plus a family supplement of 155 euros per month
The scholarship must not be repaid

records.application_route: International students and doctoral candidates from abroad apply either through the HSS Auslandsbüro in their home country or through the online application portal, during the 15 December - 15 January window.
records.description: The Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung scholarship programme supports students and doctoral candidates who are under 45 at application, have at least B2 German language skills verified by certificate or placement test, show above-average performance, voluntary engagement and identification with the aims of the foundation, and study full-time at a state or state-recognised German university. Study scholarships pay a maximum base of 855 euros per month plus a 300 euro study-cost flat rate, health insurance allowance up to 102 euros (35 euros nursing care) and childcare allowance of 160 euros per child; doctoral scholarships pay up to 1,750 euros per month plus 100 euros research costs and 155 euros family supplement. The scholarship does not have to be repaid. International applicants apply through the HSS office abroad in their home country or via the online application portal, between 15 December 2026 and 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET).

verification.notes: Verified on the official hss.de pages on 10 October 2026: the 'wen-suchen-wir' page confirms the international applicant criteria (under 45, German B2 or comparable verified, above-average performance, voluntary engagement, interest in politics, civic responsibility, identification with the foundation's aims, full-time study at a state or state-recognised German university); the 'bewerbung' page confirms the application periods (15 December 2026 - 15 January 2027 12:00 CET for international students and doctoral candidates from abroad; 15 June 2027 - 15 July 2027 12:00 CEST for applicants educated in Germany) and the required documents; the 'finanzielle-foerderung' page confirms the current amounts (maximum 855 euros per month base plus 300 euros study-cost flat rate, health insurance allowance up to 102 euros and 35 euros nursing care, childcare allowance 160 euros per child; doctoral maximum 1,750 euros plus 100 euros research costs and 155 euros family supplement; no repayment obligation). Note: earlier records referenced a maximum base stipend of 992 euros per month; the current live page states a maximum of 855 euros, which was used.

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung scholarship): this is a politically oriented foundation, so alongside the academic file you need a profile - under 45 at application, at least B2 German verified by certificate or placement test, above-average performance, and voluntary engagement. International students and doctoral candidates from abroad are served by the HSS office in their home country or by the online application portal, in the window 15 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET). On the money side, the current page states a maximum base of 855 euros per month for study scholarships according to BMFTR guidelines, plus a 300 euro per month study-cost flat rate that is independent of parental income (use it for learning materials, language courses, conferences and excursions), a health insurance allowance up to 102 euros and nursing care allowance up to 35 euros, and a childcare allowance of 160 euros per child. Doctoral scholars receive a higher package: up to 1,750 euros per month plus 100 euros research costs and 155 euros family supplement. There is no legal entitlement to the benefits, and the scholarship does not have to be repaid.

records.programme_name: FES Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen (Friedrich Ebert Stiftung PhD funding for foreign students)
records.deadline_note: Applications can be made until approximately 2 years before the planned submission of the dissertation; there is no fixed closing date.
records.application_cycle: Rolling admissions; applications up to about two years before planned dissertation submission
records.status_note: Applications can be made at the earliest approximately 2 years before the planned submission of the dissertation, so application is possible at an early stage of doctoral planning. The scholarship is not repayable.

coverage: Additional payments possible where required (e.g. for conference costs, study trips or childcare)

records.description: FES Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen is the Friedrich Ebert Stiftung funding programme for doctoral candidates with plans for a dissertation at or with a German institution. The scholarship grants a monthly lump sum of 1,500 euros plus a supplement for health insurance and is not repayable. It is normally granted for 3.5 years, extendable in exceptional cases, at the latest until the final examination. Applications can be made until approximately 2 years before the planned submission of the dissertation; medical applicants are excluded, and German B2 is accepted even without certificate.

verification.notes: Verified on the official Friedrich Ebert Stiftung page on 10 October 2026: monthly lump sum of 1,500 euros plus supplement for health insurance, not repayable, normally granted for 3.5 years (extendable in exceptional cases, at the latest until the final examination), open to German and foreign BA/MA graduates with plans for a dissertation at or with a German institution, applications possible until approximately 2 years before the planned submission of the dissertation, additional payments possible where required, medicine excluded, German B2 accepted even without certificate (needed even if the dissertation is written in English).

records.applicant_utility: Applicant utility (original writing for the FES Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen): this is the doctoral funding route for candidates who plan to write their dissertation at or with a German institution, and it is unusually early-friendly - you can apply at the earliest about two years before the planned submission of the dissertation, which means you can already include the scholarship in your proposal planning rather than waiting until the project is nearly finished. The package is a 1,500 euro monthly lump sum plus a health insurance supplement, it is not repayable, and it is normally granted for 3.5 years with extension possible in exceptional cases up to the final examination, so it is designed to carry a whole dissertation rather than a finishing term. Two practical gates matter: medicine is excluded, and German B2 is required even without a certificate even if the dissertation itself is written in English, so arrange a credible placement test early. Additional payments are possible where needed, which makes the FES a useful companion for conference costs, study trips or childcare.
